rationale: Seeds ['service.api.links', 'service.api.redirect', 'service.domain.codes', 'service.models', 'service.repository'] -> 10 impacted modules via the reverse import graph; routes from fastapi; migrations_needed=True; blast radius 0.684.

outcome: 10 of 23 modules impacted, 7 routes, blast radius 0.68.

rationale: Capabilities ['schema_v2', 'alias_case_fix', 'expiry', 'analytics'] decomposed from the catalog. Independent work runs in parallel (implement.migration_0002, test.regression_alias); tests and docs branch after implementation and join at review; release waits for review.
alternatives_considered: Single sequential pipeline: simpler, but slower and one failure stalls everything
One mega implement node: fewer gates, far larger blast radius per failure

rationale: Exact match first, then lower-cased match restricted to is_custom rows: keeps generated base62 codes case-sensitive while making aliases case-insensitive; Expiry evaluated at read time: no background job needed; exact to the request; In-process bounded queue + batch writer: keeps DB writes off the redirect path; drops (and counts) on overflow instead of adding latency; visitor = sha256(HMAC(secret, day) + ip + ua): unique visitors per day without storing PII; salts rotate daily so hashes cannot be joined across days; Retention purge on a timer (analytics_retention_days): compliance policy CMP-003

Additive and reversible: a nullable column and a new table with a composite (link_id, day) index for the stats queries. SQLite needs batch mode for ALTER, Postgres does not; env.py selects it. The clicks table has no IP or user-agent column by design.
alternatives_considered: Store raw IP/UA and aggregate later: rejected, violates data minimisation (CMP policy)
Separate analytics database: deferred, documented as the scaling path
outcome: Migration 0002 - links.expires_at and the clicks table, plus models

rationale: Test-first bug fix. Creates an alias as 'MyLink' and asserts it resolves at /MyLink, /mylink and /MYLINK and via the metadata endpoint. The tests_fail_first gate proves it reproduces the bug (fails with an assertion, not an error) before any production code changes.
alternatives_considered: Fix first and test after: rejected, would not prove the test detects the bug
outcome: Regression test reproducing the alias case bug (red before the fix)

rationale: Aliases are stored lower case, so normalising the requested code to lower case makes alias lookups case-insensitive.
outcome: Lower-case every code on lookup (first attempt)

rationale: Exact match first keeps generated base62 codes case-sensitive; only when that misses and the requested code is not already lower case do we look up the canonical alias, restricted to is_custom rows. Aliases are already stored lower-cased, so no data migration is needed.
alternatives_considered: Lower-case every lookup: rejected, breaks generated codes (62 -> 36 symbol space and wrong links)
Add a code_lower column: rejected, unnecessary schema change
outcome: Alias lookup falls back to the canonical lower-case alias (custom links only) (self-repair: retry feedback shows 'test_generated_codes_are_case_sensitive' failing)

rationale: Expiry is evaluated at read time against UTC now, so no scheduler is required and behaviour is exact. expires_at must be timezone-aware and in the future; PATCH with null clears it.
alternatives_considered: Background job flipping a flag: rejected, adds moving parts and a lag window
outcome: Optional expires_at on create/PATCH; expired links return 410; metadata reports is_expired

rationale: The redirect only enqueues (put_nowait) and never awaits analytics I/O; a background writer batches inserts and a purger enforces analytics_retention_days. Unique visitors use a daily-salted HMAC so no PII is stored and hashes cannot be correlated across days. Failures are counted and logged without PII and never propagate to the redirect.
alternatives_considered: FastAPI BackgroundTasks per request: rejected, no batching or back-pressure, one insert per click
External queue (Kafka/SQS): deferred, documented scaling path
outcome: Click analytics off the hot path (bounded queue + batch writer), stats endpoint, retention purge

rationale: Uses per-request client addresses through the ASGI transport to simulate distinct visitors and proves that both enqueue failures and database failures leave redirects unaffected.
alternatives_considered: Unit-test the SQL only: rejected, the contract is the HTTP response
outcome: Stats API tests (distinct visitors, referrers, UA families, window validation) and failure isolation

rationale: API reference and OpenAPI are generated from the running app, so they cannot drift from the code.
